scenes.heading: Planning inventory around seasonality and lead times

sents.d: Planning inventory around seasonality and lead times
Running out during your busiest season costs more than carrying a bit of extra stock during your slowest one.

Mapping your sales by month for even a few months of history reveals seasonal patterns most sellers underestimate — ordering enough stock ahead of a predictable busy period matters more than reacting once sales are already climbing.
Supplier lead times (especially overseas manufacturing) often run 4-8 weeks or more, so inventory planning has to work backward from your busy season, not forward from today's stock level.
For new or unpredictable products, ordering a smaller test batch before committing to a large seasonal order reduces the risk of being stuck with unsold stock if demand doesn't match expectations.

take: Order ahead of busy seasons, working back from lead times.
